text.p: Revenue from Morocco's giant steel mill Sonasid is expected to rise to 1.82 billion dirhams ($186 million) this year, 2.1 percent up from 1996 levels, Casablanca Finance Intermediation (CFI) stockbrokers said on Tuesday.

"After a slight drop in revenues last year due to sluggish business activity, we forecast that Sonasid revenues will reach 1.82 billion ($186 million) this year, up 2.1 percent over the previous year," said Ismail Douiri, a CFI market analyst.
Sonasid, which is expected to be fully privatised by the end of 1997, showed a net profit of 165.8 million dirhams in 1996, down from 175.5 million in 1995.
CFI said that sales fell five percent to 1.8 billion dirhams in 1996 compared with 1995.
Established in 1974 in the northern province of Nador, the Societe Nationale de Siderurgie (Sonasid) manufactures concrete, steel and wire rod.
One of 47 listed stocks on the Casablanca bourse, Sonasid was last traded at 569 dirhams, traders said.
